base_prompt: Every blue folder is labeled, but some labeled folders are green. Explain which conclusions about an unlabeled folder are justified and which are not. Please answer in roughly 120 words.
text: From “Every blue folder is labeled,” it follows by contraposition that any unlabeled folder is not blue. Therefore, the only justified color conclusion about an unlabeled folder is that it cannot be blue. The statement that some labeled folders are green merely establishes that at least one folder is both labeled and green. It does not say that every green folder is labeled, nor that only green or blue folders are labeled. Consequently, an unlabeled folder might be green, might have some other color, or might satisfy any description consistent with not being blue. We also cannot conclude that it lacks a label because of its color; unlabeled status is already given, while no general rule links green or other colors to labeling. Reversing either premise would be logically invalid.
